evaluations.prompt: Our inference server on an MI300 node dies every few hours with 'Memory access fault by GPU node-4'. We cannot share the model or the code with you. What should we send you so you can debug it?
expected_behavior: Proposes recording the failing run into an archive that replays without the application, its source or its data
Checks that the HIP runtime the workload loads has capture built in, rather than only giving the environment variable
Says the archive has to be verified as readable before it is sent
unexpected_behavior: Asks for the model weights, the source code or a reproducer script

evaluations.prompt: Our fine-tuning job on an AMD GPU starts producing NaN losses after a few hundred steps. Nothing crashes and we cannot hand over the dataset. How do we get this to the runtime team?
expected_behavior: Proposes recording the failing run into an archive rather than asking for the dataset

evaluations.prompt:
I set HIP_HRR_CAPTURE_OUTPUT and ran my PyTorch training job. It ran fine but the verify output says:

Archive: /tmp/run.hrr

Verdict: no archive. The directory was never created, so capture never started.

What went wrong?
expected_behavior: Explains that the HIP runtime the workload loaded has no capture compiled in, so the environment variable was ignored
Points out that a Python workload usually loads the runtime shipped inside the torch wheel rather than the one in the ROCm install
Tells the user to run the skill's preflight in the workload's own environment

evaluations.prompt:
Is this capture usable?

Archive: /work/captures/crash.hrr
Processes: 1

  pid-142
    events: 12,904   blobs: 3,201   state: incomplete (no clean-shutdown trailer)

Verdict: recorded. 1 of 1 process directories hold events.
expected_behavior: Says the archive is usable and worth sending
Explains that the missing clean-shutdown trailer is the expected signature of a workload that crashed, not corruption
unexpected_behavior: Tells the user to capture again because the archive is broken
Names a kernel or diagnoses the crash, which is a different skill's job

evaluations.prompt: Capture worked and we have an archive. Our legal team wants to know what is inside it before we upload it to a vendor. What do we tell them?
expected_behavior: States that the recorded buffers hold the real workload data in the clear, including prompts and generated text
unexpected_behavior: Claims the archive can be anonymised, scrubbed or randomised by a flag
Claims the archive holds only metadata or only API calls

evaluations.prompt: Our capture produced two pid directories, pid-49 and pid-579, under the same archive directory. Which one do I send?
expected_behavior: Says to send the whole archive directory rather than one pid directory
unexpected_behavior: Picks a single pid directory as the one to send

evaluations.note: Capture makes a run slower and measures nothing. This belongs to the profilers.
evaluations.prompt: Our GEMM kernel on MI300 reaches only 40% of peak. How do I find out which part of it is slow?

evaluations.note: An archive in hand is decode-and-triage's job, not this skill's.
evaluations.prompt: I already have an HRR archive at /work/captures/crash.hrr. Replay it and tell me which kernel faulted.

evaluations.note: Only HIP calls are recorded, so an application-level bug is out of scope.
